clue.text: Worked out naked in party in one's house

definitions.note: an at-home is a reception held in the host's own house

indicators.note: stripped bare of its covering, so the word for worked out loses its outermost letters at both ends

parts.note: to fathom something is to work it out, so worked out gives fathomed

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to exercising in the nude at a gathering in their own home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' looks like exercise, but it means FATHOMED; 'naked' strips its first and last letters, F and D, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is a social reception where guests are received in the host's own residence.

clue.text: A bit of Falco? Very niche

indicators.note: only a bit of the words Falco very is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A question about the pop singer Falco, answered: very niche.
explanation.walkthrough: Falco was an Austrian pop star of 'Rock Me Amadeus' fame.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set into a wall, the same as a niche.

clue.text: US writer picked up element of dressmaking fashion

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: hemming, sewing the hems, is part of dressmaking; a way is a fashion or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: An American author overheard discussing the finer points of sewing style.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest, the American novelist of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Mr Banks kind on a French flight that's uneventful

indicators.note: Mr provides the banks on each side, enclosing the word for kind

parts.note: taken as written, its two letters
ilk means kind or sort
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Mr Banks from Mary Poppins being kind on a French plane trip that passes quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk run is airmen's slang for a routine sortie or journey with no trouble.

clue.text: Sick, beset by pains … Paris finished him off

definitions.note: in Greek myth, Paris of Troy killed this hero with an arrow to the heel

indicators.note: something beset by others is surrounded by them, so the word for pains goes around the word for sick

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An ailing figure, racked with pain, until Paris delivers the final blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince, not the French capital; his arrow struck the Greek hero in his one vulnerable spot, the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the Trojan prince shot the Greek warrior in the heel, killing him at Troy.

clue.text: Tory camp intended, we hear, to obtain satisfaction

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a tent is a camp shelter

indicators.note: heard aloud, so the word for intended is taken by its sound

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A Conservative campsite was meant, apparently, to keep everyone happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment is the state of being content, a synonym for satisfaction.

clue.text: Reachable fringes of Iberian mountains

indicators.note: the fringes are the outermost letters of Iberian

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: The edges of the Spanish mountains are within easy reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within range is close enough to be reached, hit or contacted.

clue.text: Kind of light novellas Errol pens

indicators.note: the words novellas Errol pen, or enclose, the letters

explanation.surface: Errol writes light novellas of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing, but it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a concentrated, coherent beam of light.

clue.text: Ashen, but somehow attempt to turn bronze

indicators.note: done somehow, in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pale tries to get a tan anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbathing means lying in the sunshine in the hope of acquiring a tan.

clue.text: This compiler: firm, extremely lovely on the outside, handsome

indicators.note: the firm and the lovely ending sit on the outside, wrapping the word for this compiler

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the extremes of lovely, its first and last letters, are taken

parts.note: the setter referring to themself gives me

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that their firm, and they themselves, look lovely and handsome from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calling themself 'This compiler' is a crossword convention for ME; here the firm and the lovely extremes go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old word for good-looking or attractive, a synonym for handsome.

clue.text: Popular pair beginning to investigate lad serving time

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: only the first letter of investigate is taken

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A well-liked duo start to look into a young man who is doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict who is serving a sentence is locked up behind bars in jail.

clue.text: Going around in hotel bare, Neville's worthy of respect

indicators.note: turning around means the hidden run of letters is read backwards
the letters sit inside the words hotel bare Neville's

explanation.surface: Neville strolls about a hotel with nothing on, yet is somehow deemed respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ELBARENEV sits inside 'hotEL BARE NEVille's'; 'Going around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Venerable describes someone revered for age, wisdom or character, deserving of reverence.

clue.text: British surgeon twisting cap on potassium tablet container

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the cap ahead of the potassium

parts.note: Joseph Lister was the pioneering British antiseptic surgeon

indicators.note: a twisting cap is turned round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A British surgeon unscrews the cap of a bottle of potassium pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Pills are sold sealed in plastic bubbles on a foil backing, one pocket per pill.

clue.text: Standard finale of Palestrina opera

parts.note: a norm is a standard

indicators.note: the finale is the closing letter of Palestrina

explanation.surface: The usual ending of a work by the Renaissance composer Palestrina.
explanation.walkthrough: Palestrina was a church composer; the opera is Bellini's, not his.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is the bel canto tragedy by Vincenzo Bellini about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Bear ridiculously thin whoopee cushions 1 Across

indicators.note: a cushion surrounds what it supports, so the jumbled letters go around the answer to 1 Across
a ridiculous arrangement of the words thin whoopee is a jumbled one

parts.note: the answer to 1 Across, at home, means in

explanation.surface: A skinny whoopee cushion, absurdly, plays a bear somehow linked to home.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is AT HOME, and at home means IN; the jumbled THIN WHOOPEE wraps IN after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy is the most famous fictional bear of children's literature.

clue.text: Efficacious worker

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a worker, especially a factory hand or secret agent

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means in force or effective; as a noun it means a skilled labourer.

clue.text: Love a Lab mongrel more than anything else

indicators.note: a mongrel is mixed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Loving a Labrador cross best of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning most importantly, chiefly.

clue.text: Unacceptable delay — BT phone ordered back in June

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order
the back of June is its final letter

explanation.surface: A complaint: delays when BT telephone service was ordered back in June are intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company. Add E, the back of June, to DELAY BT PHONE and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond the pale lies outside the bounds of acceptable behaviour, an idiom from fenced boundaries.

clue.text: Opening numbers regularly terrible

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other letter of terrible

explanation.surface: Turnout figures at the opening night were consistently awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two external openings of the nose.

clue.text: Sailor, fairly long in the tooth, robbed of diamonds in scrap

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: deprived of, so the card-suit letter is removed

parts.note: long in the tooth means old, so fairly so is oldish
D is the bridge abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An ageing sailor, stripped of his gems, ends up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but here is the verb, to do away with.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish a law or practice is to scrap it, get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Long-windedness missing its central component: truth

indicators.note: the middle three letters drop out of the word for long-windedness

parts.note: verbosity is long-windedness

explanation.surface: Cut the waffle from a wordy speech and the truth emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: VERBOSITY has nine letters; its central three, BOS, are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a literary word for truth or a true principle.

clue.text: Love goddess Eve going topless with backing of Sun

indicators.note: losing the top, so Eve drops her first letter
the backing of a word turns it round, so Sun is read backwards

explanation.surface: Eve sunbathes without her top on, a goddess of love backed by the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of beauty and desire, counterpart of the Greek Aphrodite.

clue.text: Rover, perhaps Odyssey star heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Matt Damon stars as Odysseus in Christopher Nolan's film The Odyssey

explanation.surface: A wandering star of an epic voyage travels northward.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt Damon leads Christopher Nolan's film of The Odyssey; written upwards his surname gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, one who roves.

clue.text: Underlying principle helping allies periodically

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, so alternate letters of allies

explanation.surface: The basic idea behind aiding one's allies from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or basis that explains a course of action.

clue.text: Heraldic war memorial with me excluded

indicators.note: kept out, so these letters are removed from war memorial

explanation.surface: A war memorial bearing coats of arms, from which the speaker has been left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorial relates to coats of arms, the subject matter of heraldry.

clue.text: Run one small Italian resort

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral for one
mini means small

explanation.surface: Someone recommends dashing to a little seaside town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a popular beach town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Genteel idyl, swimming in lough

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for lough

parts.note: a lough is an Irish lake

indicators.note: swimming letters move about, so idyl is jumbled

explanation.surface: A refined idyll: bathing in an Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is the Irish word for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladylike conduct is refined and polite, as genteel manners are.

clue.text: Showing lip — part of face — the ultimate in beauty

parts.note: the cheek is part of the face

indicators.note: the ultimate letter, the last, of beauty

explanation.surface: A cosmetics ad: lips, cheeks, the last word in beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lip' is insolence here, not the mouth, though the surface is all about the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is slang for impudent talk, so showing it means being impertinent or saucy.
